narrative:
The model predicted a 53% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability tipped above 50%, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

The decision was driven primarily by three pieces of information, ranked by importance. First, your plan to attend law school part-time was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Among accepted students, only 7% planned to study part-time, while 93% planned to go full-time; the model sees part-time enrollment as a meaningful risk for first-time bar success.

Second, your first-year law school grades worked in your favor. Placing in the 8th decile is noticeably stronger than the average of 6th decile among students who were admitted, and this higher early performance pulled the prediction back toward passing.

Third, your third-year grades also helped somewhat. Ranking in the 6th decile is slightly above the 5.8 average of accepted students, giving the model a modest positive signal.

Taken together, the part-time schedule outweighed the encouraging grade signals, resulting in a failure probability just over the acceptance threshold. 

To improve your chances, consider reapplying with a clear plan to attend full-time. Strengthening your LSAT score or undergraduate GPA could also help offset the part-time concern. Focus on those adjustments before the next cycle. (218 words)
